subject: LinguaHealth POC: trial scope & model shortlist
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@linguahealth.ai>, Dr. Sanjay Patel <sanjay.p@linguahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, Oct 18, 2026 at 3:02 PM PDT
Subject: LinguaHealth POC: trial scope & model shortlist

Thanks again for the productive call today — great context from the LinguaHealth team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we draft the SOW: 

Goals (what success looks like)
- Reduce triage routing errors for conversational intake by 50% compared to current rule-based flow (baseline provided).
- Acceptable latency: p95 < 350ms on our dedicated 2-GPU staging pool for the test workload.
- Multilingual quality: Spanish primary, Portuguese secondary — prefer no degradation vs. English more than ~8 points on your clinical intent evaluation.
- Hallucination tolerance: measured factuality score target >= 0.82 on the clinical QA prompt-set.

Proposed POC plan (high-level)
- Duration: 2 weeks (kickoff once SOW is agreed & data access provided).
- Deliverables: hosted trial endpoint, evaluation report (prompt set + aggregate metrics), one rollback-ready fallback model configured.
- Evaluation set: jointly built set (~300 clinical triage prompts + 150 multilingual samples).

Model shortlist (recommended)
- Primary: Llama 3 (70B), quantized profile for inference — best balance of instruction-following and multilingual fidelity.
- Cost fallback: Mistral-Instruct (7B) — lower cost, useful for burst/backup during peak load.
- Low-latency Spanish fallback: Llama 2 13B chat (optimized) — lower memory footprint for shorter-turn interactions.

Dependencies / asks from LinguaHealth
- Sample CSV with anonymized/intended fields (schema attached): data-sample-schema.csv
- Confirmation on whether any PHI will be present in the POC dataset — impacts logging & retention settings.
- Procurement point of contact for SOW / PO (cc when available).

Attachments: PoC-SOW-draft.pdf (first pass), data-sample-schema.csv

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Please confirm: success criteria above and model preferences (ok to proceed with Llama 3 primary + Mistral fallback?).
2) Procurement contact or go-ahead to send SOW for signature.
3) If you agree, we’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Monday Oct 25 to align test harness and SE responsibilities. 

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa in on the technical plan once we get a thumbs up.

—
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference

On Sun, Oct 18, 2026 at 3:02 PM Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the productive call today — great context from the LinguaHealth team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we draft the SOW: 
> 
> Goals (what success looks like)
> - Reduce triage routing errors for conversational intake by 50% compared to current rule-based flow (baseline provided).

Thanks Alex — this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Multilingual priority: Spanish first (high volume), Portuguese second. Can you confirm that the Llama 3 profile will not require extra labeled Spanish data to reach parity?
- Data sensitivity: LinguaHealth will anonymize PHI before sharing for the POC but we need confirmation on log retention defaults and whether any token-level logging can be disabled for the trial environment.
- Procurement: adding our procurement alias to this thread. They’ll expect a short SOW and a standard DPA addendum.

We’re generally good with the model shortlist — lean toward Llama 3 primary if you think it’s feasible for Spanish out-of-the-box. Please send the SOW to procurement and cc me.

Olivia Chen
Head of Product, LinguaHealth
olivia@linguahealth.ai

Internal notes & proposed assignments (moving quickly so we can respond to procurement):

SE + delivery plan (Marissa)
- Lead the test-harness setup (we'll provide a hosted endpoint + evaluation runner).
- Build multilingual evaluation pipeline: 300 English triage prompts + 120 Spanish + 60 Portuguese (Marissa will coordinate prompt translation QA).
- Verify quantized runtime for Llama 3 70B on our staging 2xA6000 pool; measure p95 for 64-token completion.

CS + success (Ben)
- Be the customer success owner for trial cadence and acceptance criteria sign-off.
- Run weekly check-ins; own the rollout gate decision with LinguaHealth.

Metrics & pass/fail thresholds (draft)
- Intent accuracy >= 82% overall, Spanish >= 74% (we can iterate).
- Hallucination rate < 3% on clinical factuality checks.
- Latency p95 < 350ms for the primary model on our staging config.
- Cost target: average inference cost under $0.015 per request for the evaluation mix (to be finalized).

Action items
1) Marissa: confirm we can get a quantized Llama 3 70B profile into staging by Oct 23 and validate p95 numbers.
2) Ben: Draft a week-by-week cadence doc and acceptance checklist; share by EOD Wed Oct 21.
3) Alex: Send SOW to procurement and schedule kickoff for Oct 25 if SOW is approved.

Attaching the sample schema that Olivia asked for — this is the CSV we asked them to populate: data-sample-schema.csv

—
Alex
